deck.title: Voice-Controlled Presentations
deck.subtitle: From a browser prototype to native PowerPoint and Keynote control
deck.author: Tantular Labs

slides.title: Voice-Controlled Presentations
body: A hands-free way to run a deck.
Push-to-talk, not always-listening.
Every command is visible before it acts.
slides.notes: Open by holding the mic button once to show a live command, then immediately show the keyboard still works. That sequencing proves the fallback story before you say a word about it.

slides.title: The Problem With Presenter Remotes
body: Clickers get lost, run out of battery, or lock to one vendor's app.
Presenters need both hands free for gestures, demos, or a whiteboard.
Speech is a natural, low-friction second input -- if it's reliable.
slides.notes: Reliability is the whole pitch. A remote that sometimes skips two slides is worse than no remote.

slides.title: Design Principles
body: Reliability before cleverness.
Push-to-talk by default -- never always-listening.
Every recognized command is shown before or as it executes.
Keyboard and buttons always work, with or without speech or a model.
slides.notes: These four principles are non-negotiable constraints, not aspirations -- they shaped every implementation decision in this deck.

slides.title: A Transport-Neutral Command Contract
body: One normalized JSON command shape: action, slide, query, source, confidence, transcript.
The same contract will drive the web deck today and PowerPoint/Keynote adapters later.
Navigation commands execute immediately; document-editing commands are out of scope.
slides.notes: Point at commandContract.js on screen if this is a live coding demo. The contract is deliberately small -- ten actions, no document mutation.

slides.title: Intent Routing: Deterministic First
body: A bilingual (Indonesian / English) keyword parser handles obvious commands locally.
An optional Ollama model is a fallback for phrasing the parser doesn't recognize.
Topic matching stays local -- notes and the full deck are never sent to a model.
slides.notes: This slide is a good goto_topic test target: say or type 'go to intent routing' and it should land here via the local keyword-score matcher, not the model.

slides.title: Rollout & Pricing
body: Phase 1 (today): free, open web MVP -- any laptop, any projector, zero install.
Phase 2: native PowerPoint and Keynote control, licensed per presenter seat.
Phase 3: offline recognition for venues with no reliable network.
slides.notes: If asked about pricing live, this is the slide to land on -- say 'go to pricing' to test the topic matcher on stage.

slides.title: Why the Web Deck Comes First
body: No install, no OS permissions, no risk to an existing PowerPoint/Keynote file.
Fastest path to validate the voice UX and the command contract with real audiences.
Everything learned here -- parsing, dedup, HUD, fallbacks -- carries into the native adapters unchanged.
slides.notes: This is the bridge slide into the native roadmap discussion -- see NATIVE_POWERPOINT_KEYNOTE_ROADMAP.md.

slides.title: Thank You
body: Questions welcome.
Try it yourself: hold Space or the mic button and say "go to pricing".
Roadmap and source: voice_deck/ in this repository.
